title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate resolution affirms that protecting religious freedom is essential, recognizing that people rely on authoritative texts for moral guidance. It also calls for greater transparency in artificial intelligence systems, ensuring that their decision‑making processes are open and accountable.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Safety Board, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes creating an Artificial Intelligence Safety Board that would oversee the development and deployment of AI systems, ensuring they meet safety and ethical standards. It also includes additional measures aimed at regulating AI usage and addressing related policy concerns.

title: A bill to require the Secretary of Defense to establish reporting requirements and voluntary guidance for large artificial intelligence contractors.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill requires the Secretary of Defense to set up reporting rules for large artificial‑intelligence contractors and to offer voluntary guidance on how they should operate. This is intended to increase transparency and oversight of AI firms that work on defense projects.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration.
summary: This resolution establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to examine AI issues and advise lawmakers. The committee will focus on responsible AI development, ethical considerations, and regulatory frameworks to guide national policy.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a legislative proposal that aims to safeguard consumers against misleading or false claims about artificial intelligence. It requires companies to clearly label AI-generated content, disclose the use of AI, and ensures transparency so consumers can make informed decisions.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a federal law that sets out strict standards and oversight for AI research to ensure the technology is safe, reliable, and trustworthy. It requires researchers to conduct thorough testing, document their methods clearly, and share findings with regulators so the public can have confidence in AI systems.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to report to Congress on how artificial intelligence systems are used to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. This report is intended to provide oversight and transparency about AI’s role in intelligence gathering.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act aims to improve AI education and prepare workers for jobs in AI‑driven industries. It proposes training programs, curriculum updates, and workforce development initiatives to build AI skills across the population.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act aims to promote transparency and collaboration in artificial intelligence development by encouraging the release of source code for AI systems. It seeks to establish guidelines and incentives for open‑source AI projects to foster innovation, reduce duplication, and ensure that AI technologies benefit the broader public.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 prohibits the use of artificial intelligence for diagnosing, treating, or making any medical decision without the direct involvement of a licensed human physician. It establishes penalties for healthcare providers who rely on AI systems for patient care without a qualified doctor’s oversight.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to curb companies from charging excessively high prices for AI services and from using AI tools to unfairly manipulate or suppress wages. It would impose new regulations and penalties on firms that engage in such practices, protecting consumers and workers from exploitation.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to create a pilot program that uses AI to defend critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. It also includes additional measures to strengthen national cyber security efforts.

title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes setting up a new Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee and investigate issues related to cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. The bill also includes other unspecified provisions aimed at improving oversight and governance in related areas.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: This bill proposes creating the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, a government program aimed at investing in AI research and development. It also includes additional provisions for related AI initiatives and oversight.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act aims to regulate the creation, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence models, ensuring they are transparent and accountable. It requires detailed auditing, safeguards for data handling, and measures to protect users from potential risks posed by advanced AI systems.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The bill seeks to protect households from the steep electric costs that power large AI data centers. It proposes limits on those energy charges, mandates transparent reporting of usage, and encourages greener power sources so families aren’t hit with hidden AI‑related fees.

title: Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act creates a federal department dedicated to advancing and overseeing AI and related technologies. It likely sets out the department’s goals, powers, and responsibilities for fostering innovation, ensuring safety, and coordinating national AI policy.

title: A bill to establish the Department of Artificial Intelligence and to provide for the regulation of advanced artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes creating a new federal Department of Artificial Intelligence that would oversee the development and use of advanced AI systems. It also outlines regulations and safeguards for those systems and includes additional provisions to coordinate AI policy across government agencies.

title: A bill to require disclosure of certain information relating to artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill requires companies that build or use artificial‑intelligence systems to provide clear, accessible disclosures about how those systems work, what data they were trained on, and any known limitations or biases. The aim is to increase transparency, help users make informed decisions, and promote safer deployment of AI technologies.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 is a law that aims to ensure AI systems used by the Department of Veterans Affairs are safe, ethical, and transparent. It requires the department to set clear guidelines for AI development, monitor how those systems perform, and protect veterans’ privacy and rights.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law aimed at limiting the creation and use of artificial intelligence systems that could pose serious safety, security, or ethical risks. It calls for strict regulations and oversight mechanisms to prevent the deployment of AI technologies deemed “rogue” or harmful.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law that aims to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in processing veterans’ claims, ensuring these systems operate transparently and fairly. It seeks to establish clear accountability standards so veterans receive accurate, unbiased decisions and can trust the VA’s AI-driven processes.

title: Covered AI Prohibition Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Covered AI Prohibition Act is a legislative proposal that bans the use of artificial intelligence in certain specified sectors or activities. Its purpose is to safeguard individuals from potential harms by limiting AI deployment in these covered areas.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act sets out standards for testing and confirming the safety and trustworthiness of AI systems used by the military. It also requires regular, transparent reporting to oversight bodies so that the use of these systems can be monitored and held accountable.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires all artificial intelligence systems used within the Department of Veterans Affairs to be fully documented, publicly disclosed, and subject to ongoing oversight. The goal is to ensure that veteran services powered by AI are transparent, explainable, and accountable, protecting veterans from opaque or unfair automated decision‑making.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act establishes new legal requirements to ensure that AI systems are designed, deployed, and monitored with robust security measures to protect against misuse and cyber threats. It outlines mandatory standards, oversight mechanisms, and reporting obligations for developers and users to improve overall AI safety and resilience.

title: Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act proposes prohibiting the use of artificial intelligence systems to automatically reject Medicare claims, ensuring that any denial must involve human oversight. This legislation aims to protect beneficiaries from algorithmic errors and promote transparency and accountability in Medicare decision-making.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes to pause the construction of new data centers built specifically for AI workloads, aiming to curb their high energy use and environmental footprint. The law would require existing facilities to be evaluated and potentially upgraded to meet stricter sustainability standards before any further expansion.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 seeks to stop people from illegally copying and selling U.S. AI models. It introduces fines, legal penalties, and enforcement tools to protect developers’ intellectual property and make model theft a serious crime.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a framework for studying how AI is used in judicial settings and sets up oversight mechanisms to ensure its fair and transparent application. The Act requires courts to report on AI deployments, creates a dedicated oversight committee, and mandates regular audits to safeguard judicial integrity.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 establishes rules for how the U.S. Small Business Administration can develop, deploy, and oversee AI technologies to help small businesses thrive. It focuses on encouraging responsible AI use, safeguarding data privacy, and ensuring all small businesses can access AI tools fairly.
